name: Ulrich Siegmund
role: AfD parliamentary co-leader in Saxony-Anhalt and 2026 state election lead candidate
summary: Siegmund advocates sharply reduced immigration, deportations, financial support for larger families and a revival of national cultural confidence. His proposals combine economic deregulation, social provision directed toward citizens and compulsory work for asylum recipients.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Prefers economic freedom over political micromanagement.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Wants less regulation and greater economic freedom.

cut-welfare.rationale: Would cut incentives for nonwork while retaining aid for involuntary need.

empower-police-military.rationale: Supports strengthening equipment for police, armed forces and deportation enforcement.

traditional-family.rationale: He said the AfD stands for the foundation of the family as the elementary foundation of society.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Explicitly defends inherited culture, traditions and values.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Rejects recruiting additional foreign workers as the long-term solution.

nation-first.rationale: Makes German interests the central foreign-policy test.

open-borders.rationale: Demands an immediate end to uncontrolled migration.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Dismisses regional climate measures as addressing a remote future instead of present priorities.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He told the Landtag to go back to nuclear energy and to postpone or scrap the coal exit, and later blamed the CDU for the nuclear exit.

central-planning.rationale: He described growing planned-economy interventions in normal economic structures as a cause of falling money value.

basic-income.rationale: He called the citizen's income a step toward an unconditional basic income, which he presented as a dream of the left and rejected.

democracy-best.rationale: Calls himself a democrat and accepts losing the majority vote.

direct-votes.rationale: Proposes Swiss-style popular votes on major decisions.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Treats deindustrialization as a major danger to reverse.

restore-past-order.rationale: Campaigns to recover an older, secure Germany.

conscription.rationale: Speaking for his group he said the AfD was the only one that wanted to keep conscription.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: He attacked the 2025 federal debt package as the largest in the republic's history and said the debt brake had been promised before the election.

national-self-determination.rationale: He said each nation-state knows best for its own people and culture and that this freedom should be given back to the European countries.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Would redirect benefits from unauthorized migrants toward citizens and taxpayers; accepts some distinctions among eligible migrants.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Demands compulsory work for able asylum-benefit recipients.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He asked to postpone or abolish the coal exit and praised cheap Russian gas by pipeline, which backs fossil supply, though he spoke of coal rather than new domestic drilling.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Accuses established parties of insulated, self-serving politics.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Calls the people sovereign beyond election day.

population-transfer.rationale: Reported calls to pressure foreign restaurants and make migrants leave are disputed; he limits his stated policy to unlawful residence, crime and abuse of benefits.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Objects to citizenship after five years as devaluation.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He wants a Europe of strong sovereign nation states, calls the EU a failed central state and asks how much more sovereignty is to be given up to Brussels, while accepting a trade and peace association.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Opposes spending aid abroad while domestic needs remain unmet.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Explicitly commits himself as premier to legal constraints.

common-currency.rationale: Rejects grouping divergent economies into one currency.

patriotic-education.rationale: Wants history teaching to foster cultural and historical pride.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Presenting the AfD pension points he said politicians should pay into the statutory pension insurance, which keeps the state pay-as-you-go scheme.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Proposes family loans and financial rewards instead of relying on immigration.

non-intervention.rationale: Opposes involvement in foreign wars and urges respect for other states’ interests.

public-access-to-information.rationale: He objected that answers to the AfD major inquiry were put under secrecy and said all information should be brought to the public.

socialized-care.rationale: Calls for free public kindergarten provision.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: He answered an accusation of hostility to homosexuals by saying the AfD would guarantee that everyone lives safe, free and self-determined, and contrasted Qatar's death penalty for homosexuals with his own side.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Supports domestic defense production and Bundeswehr equipment.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Supports national defense while opposing equipment sent into other countries’ wars.

pollution-taxes.rationale: He demanded that the CO2 tax and other "ideological levies" be dropped at once and blamed the CDU for introducing it.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: He accused the government of circumventing its own debt brake through an unconstitutional Corona special fund and attacked the 2025 debt package after a debt-brake campaign.

public-service-media.rationale: Would end compulsory fees, retaining basic factual broadcasting with optional subscriptions.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: He set the AfD's freedom for cars, jobs and cheap energy against restrictions by "climate hysteria".

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: He objected to dropping German as a requirement for citizenship and said language is the key to integration.

notes:
No views are inferred from AfD membership, relatives or associates. CORRECTIV’s account of his Potsdam remarks is recorded together with his denial; Sellner’s proposals are not attributed to him. His later interviews distinguish citizenship from ancestry and deny proposing unlawful expulsions. Refusal to rank the Holocaust against other crimes does not by itself establish denial of historical events. Homeschooling subject to examinations is not evidence for publicly funded school vouchers. Personal preference for small-town life is not a claim that all rural life is morally superior. Ending compulsory broadcasting fees is qualified by his proposed basic information service. His stated support for constitutional legality is distinguished from legal scholars’ objections to proposed measures. Other politicians’ remarks and journalists’ podcast commentary are excluded.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 16 answers taken from it, 18 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass, built mainly on his own speeches in the Landtag plenary protocols of the 8th term (2021-2026), downloaded and searched by theme (about 580 speeches). Themes searched: economy and welfare, taxes, pensions, health care, energy and climate, EU and euro, sanctions and Russia, defence and conscription, migration, citizenship, family, homosexuality, media, elections and referendums, courts, federalism, hate speech, weapons. His speeches centre on Corona, energy, migration and social spending, so government (courts, referendums, federalism, elections) and many liberty topics found no stated position and stay null; no answer rests on party membership or on a government's acts. The reported 2023 Potsdam meeting is not used: only his own Landtag account of remigration (offenders, illegal residents, not integrated migrants or German citizens) is recorded. Remigration is read through that account only.
